title: Kernel impedance mapper and staged autotune for prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe inconsistent latency/cost tradeoffs across GPUs and sequence lengths. Existing kernel pickers choose kernels primarily by mean latency heuristics and per-op microbenchmarks; this leads to suboptimal tail latency and cost for mixed prefill+decode workloads and for heterogeneous fleets (A100, L40, H100 variants).

Goal: Build a lightweight, explainable 'kernel impedance' score and a staged autotuning workflow that: 1) quantifies kernel suitability per (arch, seqlen, batch, op-mode), 2) safely explores better kernels during low-risk windows, and 3) integrates with prefill/decode handshake to avoid prefills that increase tail latency.

High-level approach:
- Kernel impedance mapper: aggregate microbenchmarks + live telemetry into a single impedance score combining 50th/90th/99th latency, memory occupancy, and cost-per-token. Normalize across architectures via a small arch-normalization transform. Score is intentionally conservative (bias toward lower tail latency).
- Staged autotune: three phases: seed (offline microbench fingerprinting), probe (small % of live requests routed as probes with telemetry collection), and adopt/rollback (apply new kernel candidate to broader traffic with automatic rollback criteria based on tail and error signals).
- Prefill/decode handshake: when a kernel candidate increases prefill cost or KV cache variance, prefer scheduling probes during background-prefill windows or use ephemeral warm caches to avoid contaminating decode latency. Add a prefetch budget per request class to limit warmstart overhead.

Success criteria:
- 10-15% reduction in 95th-token latency for mixed prefill/decode SLO-sensitive routes in Canary region compared to baseline.
- No more than 2% increase in per-token cost for routes flagged as cost-sensitive.
- Safe automatic rollback observed in canary runs for any candidate that increases 99th percentile latency beyond configured SLOs.

Telemetry & metrics:
- new timeseries: kernel_impedance_score{arch,model,seqlen,route} (0-100), probe_success_rate, probe_tail_latency, per_token_cost_by_kernel.
acceptance_criteria: Impedance score computed and visible in runtime metrics for at least 3 kernel variants across two architectures (A100, L40)
Staged probe pipeline running in Canary with <1% of traffic routed as probes and telemetry persisted to metrics DB
Automatic rollback triggers correctly when 99th-token latency increases above configured threshold
Documentation for operations and an operator runbook for forcing fallback applied
implementation_steps: Design impedance score formula and arch-normalization transform (RFC)
Extend microbench harness to emit occupancy and 99th latency for seqlen buckets
Add lightweight in-runtime probe router with sampling and isolated KV cache behavior
Wire telemetry into existing metrics pipeline and dashboards (Grafana panels for impedance by route)
Canary rollout of probe candidates with rollback policy; run 2 week experiment
Postmortem and tuning: adjust scoring weights and probe budgets based on canary results
risks: Probes may perturb production caches if not isolated; mitigated by ephemeral/isolated warm cache option
Cross-arch normalization might hide real performance differences; must preserve arch labels for debugging
Exploration budget too aggressive could increase cost for high-throughput routes; enforce per-route budgets
qa_plan: Unit tests for score computation and edge cases (zero division, missing telemetry)
Simulated workload tests with replay traffic to validate no decode tail regressions
Canary monitoring dashboards with alerting for probe_tail_latency and probe_error_rate
Manual QA on Dedicated cluster with heterogeneous GPUs to validate arch-normalization
